title: Ashok Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P.
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Chandra Kumar Rai, J.
disposition: Second writ for the same Clause 6.5 bill-correction relief dismissed; alleged non-compliance of the earlier order is to be pursued by contempt.
headnote: A second writ seeking correction of an electricity bill is not maintainable where an earlier writ for the same relief has already been disposed of with liberty to approach the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Alleged failure to supply a corrected bill in compliance with that order is to be pursued by contempt, not by a fresh writ.
facts: Ashok Kumar Gupta approached the Allahabad High Court a second time seeking correction of his electricity bill. The same relief had already been claimed in Writ-C No. 17001 of 2022, disposed of on 14 June 2022 with liberty to approach the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Counsel submitted that a correct bill had still not been supplied in compliance with that order. Counsel for the respondents was heard.

holding_units.topic: second writ after Clause 6.5 remittal; contempt for non-compliance
holding_units.holding: A second writ seeking the same electricity-bill correction already remitted to the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is not maintainable. Non-supply of a corrected bill in alleged non-compliance of the earlier order is to be pursued by contempt, not by a fresh writ for the same relief.

principle_tags.application: After an earlier writ had remitted bill-correction to Clause 6.5, the Court refused to re-decide the bill on a second writ and left alleged non-compliance to be pursued by contempt.

not_decided.point: correctness of the electricity bill and compliance with the 14.06.2022 Clause 6.5 order
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the bill or whether the licensee had complied with the earlier remittal; it dismissed the second writ and pointed the petitioner to contempt.
